_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Uganda is the first of two East Africa remainder countries (AF/G.8 priority 2, alongside Rwanda) -- the docx's own country list is exhausted, so this is from-scratch primary research like Lesotho/Eswatini/Zambia/Malawi/Zimbabwe before it. Researched by a subagent this session, all findings independently structured as Part A quote records before being minted here. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review, following the established DRAFT-then-import pattern.
_note: Uganda's own CPI documents are notably silent on every external framework this branch has come to expect a citation to: the March 2026 and July 2021 UBOS CPI releases were both searched in full for 'East African Community'/'EAC', 'IMF', and 'SNA' and none appear anywhere -- a genuine silence, not a hedge, and a contrast with Tanzania's and Kenya's CPI documents, which both name the EAC HCPI guidelines/regulations directly. The EAC's own regulation document names Uganda as a founding Partner State, but that citation runs the opposite direction (EAC naming Uganda, not Uganda naming EAC) and per the corpus's own direction rule cannot support an edge from Uganda's CPI to `eac-hcpi-regulations`. On social protection: the Senior Citizens Grant's decade-long nominal freeze (2010-2020, per the World Bank) and subsequent ad hoc increase (UGX 25,000 to UGX 35,000, reported only in secondary news coverage, for FY2026/27) is the same shape found repeatedly elsewhere in this branch -- a fixed transfer amount raised occasionally without any stated formula -- but Uganda's own government social-protection policy and strategy documents (2016 and 2025) are, unusually, completely silent on inflation/CPI/erosion language; the only explicit statement of erosion found anywhere is in a World Bank assessment, not a Government of Uganda document. That is a genuine difference in shape from Tanzania's, Malawi's and Eswatini's own admissions in their own policy documents.

_open_questions.question: The Public Service Pension Fund Act, 2025 was reported by URBRA (Uganda Retirement Benefits Regulatory Authority) and by Makerere University's own retirement benefits scheme trustees to have introduced a new contributory public-service pension scheme (5% employee / 10% employer contributions), but this session could not locate the Act's own primary text -- it appears too recent to be indexed on ULII or similar legal databases. Whether it contains any CPI/inflation-linked benefit-adjustment provision is unconfirmed.

NTV Uganda (a news outlet, not a primary source) reports the Senior Citizens Grant/SAGE amount rising from UGX 25,000 to UGX 35,000 effective FY2026/27, but gives no indication of a formula or CPI-linked rationale. No Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development or Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development budget document confirming this figure or its rationale was located this session.

The 2022-consolidated text of the National Social Security Fund Act (https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/1985/8/eng@2022-01-07) returned a bot-verification block to every fetch attempt this session. Section 35's interest-rate mechanism was confirmed against the 2000-consolidated text and against the SSA/ISSA country profile, but whether the 2022 revision changed this provision is unconfirmed.

reports.title: Uganda Consumer Price Index (2016/17=100)
reports.description: UBOS's monthly Consumer Price Index release for Uganda (Composite) and ten urban centres. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the March 2026 edition, cross-checked against the July 2021 edition for stability of wording. Foreword: 'The current Consumer Price Index has been rebased from 2009/2010 to 2016/2017, using weights derived from the Uganda National Household Survey (UNHS VI) that was conducted from July 2016 to June 2017.' Classification: 'The rebased CPI is classified using international standards, referred to as Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP 2018) This is a shift from the COICOP 1999 that was used in the earlier series.' Formula: 'At the elementary aggregate (EA) level, the indices are computed using the Jevons (Geometric Mean) method for all items within the elementary aggregates. The modified Laspeyres index formula is used to compute higher level indices.' Both the March 2026 and July 2021 editions were searched in full for 'East African Community'/'EAC', 'IMF', 'SNA' and 'System of National Accounts' -- none appear anywhere, a genuine silence rather than a hedge, and a contrast with Tanzania's and Kenya's own CPI documents.

release_schedule.note: UBOS could not be fetched directly (robots.txt blocked WebFetch access), so this is based on the consistent monthly pattern of UBOS CPI report pages (e.g. consumer-price-index-december-2025, -january-2026 through -july-2026, one per month, published near month-end) plus a third-party economic calendar (TradingEconomics) that lists UBOS CPI releases occurring at the end of each month and shows the next one scheduled for 2026-08-28. Exact day-of-month varies slightly (e.g. July 2026 release was on 2026-07-31); day given for the next entry is from the aggregator's calendar, not confirmed directly on ubos.org.

reports.title: Uganda National Household Survey 2016/2017 (UNHS VI)
reports.description: The sixth round of Uganda's National Household Survey, 'conducted from July 2016 to June 2017' (per the CPI release's own Foreword), whose expenditure data supply the weights currently used in the rebased Uganda CPI. A recurring, titled survey series (UNHS I-VI to date), the same node shape as Tanzania's Household Budget Survey and Kenya's rebasing-report weight source, minted here as its own node rather than folded into the CPI's description because it is independently named with its own round number and dates.
reports.cadence_note: Conducted roughly every 3 years; UNHS VI covered July 2016-June 2017.

release_schedule.note: UNHS VI (2016/17) is one specific past edition in a recurring UBOS survey series (UNHS), not itself a repeating publication. There is no published calendar or stated periodicity rule; UBOS has run rounds at irregular ~3-4 year intervals: 2016/17 (VI, report published 2018), 2019/20 (VII, report published 2021), 2023/24 (VIII, report released 15 May 2025 per https://www.ubos.org/uganda-national-household-survey-report-2023-2024-released/), and the 'Ninth Uganda National Household Survey (UNHS) 2026/2027' which was in enumerator-training/field-testing stage as of mid-July 2026 (https://nilepost.co.ug/news/356326/ubos-trains-80-data-collectors-ahead-of-20262027-national-household-survey, https://allafrica.com/stories/202607160614.html). No article specifies the fieldwork end date or report release date for this ninth round. Based on the observed lag between fiscal-year end and report release in the prior three rounds (roughly 10-14 months after the FY ends in June), the report for the 2026/2027 round is projected to appear in the first half of 2028; this projected date is an inference (implied), not a published date.

reports.title: Uganda Economic Update, 14th Edition: Strengthening Social Protection to Reduce Vulnerability and Promote Inclusive Growth
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (February 2020). On the Senior Citizens Grant (SCG): 'The nominal transfer value of the SCG has not been adjusted since the scheme started in 2010. Given significant inflation over the last decade, the benefit's real value has declined by about 40 percent since 2010 (Figure 19)... If the SCG, as well as other transfers such as those provided through NUSAF, are not indexed for inflation, there is a risk that the transfer value will become too little to have any meaningful impact on recipients.' States the SCG amount at the time as 'a grant of USh 25,000 which is paid every two months' -- a figure since increased (see _note) without any stated formula. This is a World Bank staff assessment of Uganda's own programme, not a Government of Uganda document -- Uganda's own social-protection policy and strategy documents (ug-national-social-protection-policy-2016, ug-national-social-protection-strategy-2025) contain no equivalent admission, unlike Tanzania's or Malawi's own policy documents.
reports.cadence_note: Nominally twice-yearly per the World Bank's own description ("a twice-yearly analysis of the country's recent economic performance"), though actual publication has run more frequent in some years — three editions inside calendar year 2025 alone (24th: Feb, 25th: Sep, 26th: Dec).

entries.covers: Next Uganda Economic Update edition (27th/28th) after the 26th Edition (Dec 24, 2025)

release_schedule.rule: "The Uganda Economic Update, now in its 26th edition, is a twice-yearly analysis of the country's recent economic performance and near-term macroeconomic outlook." (World Bank, Uganda Economic Update 26th Edition page)
release_schedule.note: This is a stated periodicity, not a fixed-date calendar. The series has actually been publishing more often than the corpus's current 0.5/year figure suggests: confirmed recent editions are 24th (Feb 24, 2025), 25th (Sep 30, 2025), and 26th (Dec 24, 2025) — three editions inside calendar year 2025 alone. A World Bank openknowledge.worldbank.org record titled "Uganda Economic Update, June 2026" also turned up in search (page itself returned 403 on fetch, so its exact date/edition number could not be independently verified), which would be consistent with the 6-month cadence and would already be in the past relative to today (2026-08-11); if that edition already happened, the next one is more likely toward Q4 2026 (~Dec, matching the 2024/2025 December releases). Given the imprecision, this entry uses a half-year window (H2 2026) rather than a fabricated exact date.

reports.title: The Uganda National Social Protection Policy
reports.publisher: Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (Uganda)
reports.description: Uganda's framework social-protection policy (2015/2016), establishing the Senior Citizens Grant (SCG) and Vulnerable Family Grant (VFG) under the SAGE (Social Assistance Grants for Empowerment) programme. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session -- searched in full for 'inflation', 'Consumer Price Index', 'CPI', 'cost of living', 'indexation' and 'erosion': none appear anywhere. A documented silence, not a denial -- the Policy establishes the grants without discussing whether or how their value is protected against inflation.
reports.cadence_note: A multi-year policy framework, not a recurring release.

release_schedule.note: The policy document itself states measures 'shall be evaluated at midterm and after 10 years to establish impact, gaps, emerging issues and challenges' (policy dated July 2016), but this is an internal M&E provision, not a commitment to publish a revised or successor policy document on a fixed date. No publisher calendar, statute, or stated republication rule was found, and no distinct newer edition of the policy itself was located (only a re-hosted copy of the same document appears on mglsd.go.ug/policies/, linked via a 2021-dated URL path but identical in title/content to the 2016 PDF). This confirms the existing cadence_note's characterization as a multi-year policy framework rather than a recurring release.

reports.title: The National Social Protection Strategy
reports.publisher: Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (Uganda)
reports.description: Uganda's current social-protection strategy (February 2025), confirming the Senior Citizens Grant's continued rollout: 'piloting of the Senior Citizens Grant targeting older persons aged 60 years in Karamoja region and 65 years and above in the rest of the country.' VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session -- searched in full for 'inflation', 'Consumer Price Index', 'CPI', 'cost of living', 'indexation', 'erosion of benefit value', 'benefit level', 'benefit value', 'review of benefit' and 'adequacy': none appear anywhere. Notably, even this 2025 document does not repeat or update the World Bank's 2020 finding of 40 percent real-value erosion (ug-worldbank-economic-update-14) -- the silence persists five years later in Uganda's own most recent strategic document.
reports.cadence_note: A multi-year strategy document, not a recurring release.

release_schedule.note: The National Social Protection Strategy 2024-2029 is a multi-year strategic document covering a 5-year period (2024-2029), published February 2025. The document does not state any formal review cycle or fixed timeline for producing a successor strategy; no publisher release calendar exists for this title. This confirms the existing cadence_note's characterization as a non-recurring, multi-year strategy document.

reports.title: The National Social Security Fund Act, Cap. 222
reports.description: Uganda's main contributory provident-fund statute for private-sector workers. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (2000-consolidated text; the 2022-consolidated text was blocked by a bot-verification wall -- see _open_questions). Section 35(1)-(2): 'interest at the rate declared by the Minister calculated on the balance standing to the credit of the account of the member of the fund on the first day of the financial year shall be added to the account' and 'the Minister shall after consultation with the board declare the rate of interest for that financial year which shall be the rate applicable to every account,' with a default floor of 2.5 percent under s.35(3) if no rate is declared. This is a Minister-set, investment-return-based rate, not a CPI-linked one -- corroborated independently by the SSA/ISSA 'Social Security Programs Throughout the World: Africa, 2019' country profile for Uganda: 'The annual interest rate is based on the rate of return on National Social Security Fund investments and is set in consultation with the Minister of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development.'
reports.cadence_note: A standing statute, not a recurring release.

release_schedule.note: This is a standing statute (Cap. 222) maintained by Parliament of Uganda / ULII, not a periodic release. It is amended irregularly as Parliament sees fit -- e.g. National Social Security Fund (Amendment) Act, 2021 and National Social Security Fund (Amendment) Act, 2022 (consolidated at ulii.org/akn/ug/act/1985/8/eng@2022-01-07). No release calendar, stated periodicity rule, or consistent time-of-year amendment pattern exists.
